VERDICT: ACCEPT

The final answer N(N+1)/2 is plausible and matches what I recall of the result in the literature on rational solutions of the massive Thirring model, though I could not verify it against the source here. The proposed argument has a sound structure: if the denominator has degree N(N+1) and its zeros come in complex-conjugate pairs with none on the real axis, exactly half of them lie in the upper half-plane. The check for N=1 is consistent, since the first algebraic soliton gives one pole in the upper half-plane. The weak point is the unjustified claim that the degree is N(N+1), which I did not derive from the double-Wronskian construction.

CONFIDENCE: 3
